                                                                                          R-package with shiny interface, provides a framework for\nthe analysis of transcriptomics, proteomics and/or metabolomics\ndata. The interface offers a guided experience for the user,\nfrom the definition of the experimental design to the\nintegration of several omics table together. A report can be\ngenerated with all settings and analysis results.
#> 412                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 TreeAndLeaf implements a hybrid layout strategy that\nenhances leaf-level visualization in dendrograms. By\nintegrating force-directed graph and tree layout algorithms, it\nenables projection of multiple layers of information onto\ngraph–tree diagrams.
#> 413                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     RedeR combines an R package with a stand-alone Java\napplication for interactive visualization and manipulation of\nnested networks. Graph, node, and edge attributes can be\nconfigured using either graphical or command-line methods,\nfollowing igraph syntax rules.
#> 414                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             MIRit is an R package that provides several methods for\ninvestigating the relationships between miRNAs and genes in\ndifferent biological conditions. In particular, MIRit allows to\nexplore the functions of dysregulated miRNAs, and makes it\npossible to identify miRNA-gene regulatory axes that control\nbiological pathways, thus enabling the users to unveil the\ncomplexity of miRNA biology. MIRit is an all-in-one framework\nthat aims to help researchers in all the central aspects of an\nintegrative miRNA-mRNA analyses, from differential expression\nanalysis to network characterization.
#> 415                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    BreastSubtypeR provides an assumption-aware, multi-method\nframework for intrinsic molecular subtyping of breast cancer.\nThe package harmonizes several published nearest-centroid (NC)\nand single-sample predictor (SSP) classifiers, supplies\nmethod-specific preprocessing and robust probe-to-gene mapping,\nand implements a cohort-aware AUTO mode that selectively\nenables classifiers compatible with the cohort composition. A\nlocal Shiny app (iBreastSubtypeR) is included for interactive\nanalyses and to support users without programming experience.
#> 416                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Framework for processing and visualization of\nchromatographically separated and single-spectra mass spectral\ndata. Imports from AIA/ANDI NetCDF, mzXML, mzData and mzML\nfiles. Preprocesses data for high-throughput, untargeted\nanalyte profiling.
#> 417                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Uses platform-specific implemenations of the GatingML2.0\nstandard to exchange gated cytometry data with other software\nplatforms.
#> 418                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This package estimates tumor purity, copy number, and loss\nof heterozygosity (LOH), and classifies single nucleotide\nvariants (SNVs) by somatic status and clonality. PureCN is\ndesigned for targeted short read sequencing data, integrates\nwell with standard somatic variant detection and copy number\npipelines, and has support for tumor samples without matching\nnormal samples.
#> 419                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Fit a latent embedding multivariate regression (LEMUR)\nmodel to multi-condition single-cell data. The model provides a\nparametric description of single-cell data measured with\ntreatment vs. control or more complex experimental designs. The\nparametric model is used to (1) align conditions, (2) predict\nlog fold changes between conditions for all cells, and (3)\nidentify cell neighborhoods with consistent log fold changes.\nFor those neighborhoods, a pseudobulked differential expression\ntest is conducted to assess which genes are significantly\nchanged.
#> 420                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        svaRetro contains functions for detecting retrotransposed\ntranscripts (RTs) from structural variant calls. It takes\nstructural variant calls in GRanges of breakend notation and\nidentifies RTs by exon-exon junctions and insertion sites. The\ncandidate RTs are reported by events and annotated with\ninformation of the inserted transcripts.
#> 421                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Implements a variety of methods for combining p-values in\ndifferential analyses of genome-scale datasets. Functions can\ncombine p-values across different tests in the same analysis\n(e.g., genomic windows in ChIP-seq, exons in RNA-seq) or for\ncorresponding tests across separate analyses (e.g., replicated\ncomparisons, effect of different treatment conditions). Support\nis provided for handling log-transformed input p-values,\nmissing values and weighting where appropriate.
#> 422                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  RTNsurvival integrates regulons inferred by the RTN\npackage with survival data. For each regulon, a two-tailed GSEA\nframework computes a differential Enrichment Score (dES) at the\nindividual-sample level. The resulting dES distribution across\nsamples is then used to evaluate survival associations within\nthe cohort. Two primary workflows are supported: (i) Cox\nproportional hazards models, in which regulon activities are\ntreated as predictors of survival time, and (ii) Kaplan–Meier\nanalyses assessing cohort stratification based on regulon\nactivity. All graphical outputs are customizable according to\nuser specifications.
#> 423                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        RTNduals identifies co-regulatory loops between pairs of\nregulons inferred by the RTN package by evaluating their shared\ntarget genes. It infers dual regulons and tests whether\nregulator pairs exhibit cooperative or competitive influences\non common targets.
#> 424                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   A transcriptional regulatory network (TRN) consists of a\ncollection of transcription factors (TFs) and the regulated\ntarget genes. TFs are regulators that recognize specific DNA\nsequences and guide the expression of the genome, either\nactivating or repressing the expression the target genes. The\nset of genes controlled by the same TF forms a regulon. This\npackage provides classes and methods for the reconstruction of\nTRNs and analysis of regulons.
#> 425                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Provides visualization functionality for untargeted LC-MS\nmetabolomics research. Includes quality control visualizations,\nfeature-wise visualizations and results visualizations.
#> 426                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Mutational processes leave characteristic footprints in\ngenomic DNA. This package provides a comprehensive set of\nflexible functions that allows researchers to easily evaluate\nand visualize a multitude of mutational patterns in base\nsubstitution catalogues of e.g. healthy samples, tumour\nsamples, or DNA-repair deficient cells. The package covers a\nwide range of patterns including: mutational signatures,\ntranscriptional and replicative strand bias, lesion\nsegregation, genomic distribution and association with genomic\nfeatures, which are collectively meaningful for studying the\nactivity of mutational processes. The package works with single\nnucleotide variants (SNVs), insertions and deletions (Indels),\ndouble base substitutions (DBSs) and larger multi base\nsubstitutions (MBSs). The package provides functionalities for\nboth extracting mutational signatures de novo and determining\nthe contribution of previously identified mutational signatures\non a single sample level. MutationalPatterns integrates with\ncommon R genomic analysis workflows and allows easy association\nwith (publicly available) annotation data.
#> 427                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   CARD is a reference-based deconvolution method that\nestimates cell type composition in spatial transcriptomics\nbased on cell type specific expression information obtained\nfrom a reference scRNA-seq data. A key feature of CARD is its\nability to accommodate spatial correlation in the cell type\ncomposition across tissue locations, enabling accurate and\nspatially informed cell type deconvolution as well as refined\nspatial map construction. CARD relies on an efficient\noptimization algorithm for constrained maximum likelihood\nestimation and is scalable to spatial transcriptomics with tens\nof thousands of spatial locations and tens of thousands of\ngenes.
#> 428                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Provides `dplyr` verbs (`mutate`, `select`, `filter`,\netc...) supporting `S4Vectors::DataFrame` objects. Importantly,\nthis is achieved without conversion to an intermediate\n`tibble`. Adds grouping infrastructure to `DataFrame` which is\nrespected by the transformation verbs.
#> 429                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           cfDNA fragments carry important features for building\ncancer sample classification ML models, such as fragment size,\nand fragment end motif etc. Analyzing and visualizing fragment\nsize metrics, as well as other biological features in a\ncurated, standardized, scalable, well-documented, and\nreproducible way might be time intensive. This package intends\nto resolve these problems and simplify the process. It offers\ntwo sets of functions for cfDNA feature characterization and\nvisualization.
#> 430                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            sRACIPE implements a randomization-based method for gene\ncircuit modeling. It allows us to study the effect of both the\ngene expression noise and the parametric variation on any gene\nregulatory circuit (GRC) using only its topology, and simulates\nan ensemble of models with random kinetic parameters at\nmultiple noise levels. Statistical analysis of the generated\ngene expressions reveals the basin of attraction and stability\nof various phenotypic states and their changes associated with\nintrinsic and extrinsic noises. sRACIPE provides a holistic\npicture to evaluate the effects of both the stochastic nature\nof cellular processes and the parametric variation.
#> 431                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Utility package to facilitate integration and analysis of\nEBI MGnify data in R. The package can be used to import\nmicrobial data for instance into TreeSummarizedExperiment\n(TreeSE). In TreeSE format, the data is directly compatible\nwith miaverse framework.
#> 432                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          BLASE is a method for finding where bulk RNA-seq data lies\non a single-cell pseudotime trajectory. It uses a fast and\nunderstandable approach based on Spearman correlation, with\nbootstrapping to provide confidence. BLASE can be used to\n"date" bulk RNA-seq data, annotate cell types in scRNA-seq, and\nhelp correct for developmental phenotype differences in bulk\nRNA-seq experiments.
#> 433                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 High-throughput extensible toolkit for processing FASTQ\ndata. The goal of this package is to empower users to quickly\nbuild out small programmatic 'kernels' to define any FASTQ\nprocessing task they may need. Builds on Intel TBB’s flow graph\nto orchestrate concurrent I/O and data processing; throughput\ncan be as fast as compression and disk speed allows. The\npackage also ships with a suite of predefined kernels for\ncommon FASTQ tasks.
#> 434                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Implements statistical & computational tools for analyzing\nmass spectrometry imaging datasets, including methods for\nefficient pre-processing, spatial segmentation, and\nclassification.
#> 435                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Implements exact and approximate methods for nearest\nneighbor detection, in a framework that allows them to be\neasily switched within Bioconductor packages or workflows.\nExact searches can be performed using the k-means for k-nearest\nneighbors algorithm, vantage point trees, or an exhaustive\nsearch. Approximate searches can be performed using the Annoy\nor HNSW libraries. Each search can be performed with a variety\nof different distance metrics, parallelization, and variable\nnumbers of neighbors. Range-based searches (to find all\nneighbors within a certain distance) are also supported.
#> 436                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  TaxSEA is an R package for Taxon Set Enrichment Analysis,\nwhich utilises a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test analyses to\ninvestigate differential abundance analysis output for whether\nthere are alternations in a-priori defined sets of taxa from\npublic databases (BugSigDB, MiMeDB, GutMGene, mBodyMap, BacDive\nand GMRepoV2) and collated from the literature. TaxSEA takes as\ninput a list of taxonomic identifiers (e.g. species names, NCBI\nIDs etc.) and a rank (E.g. fold change, correlation\ncoefficient). TaxSEA be applied to any microbiota taxonomic\nprofiling technology (array-based, 16S rRNA gene sequencing,\nshotgun metagenomics & metatranscriptomics etc.) and enables\nresearchers to rapidly contextualize their findings within the\nbroader literature to accelerate interpretation of results.

README.rst\n\n* import jsonlite\n\n* fix .onload\n\ndefer the message to .onattach as per guidance\n\n* import URLencode\n\n* add documentation...\n\n...for ontology(M) where M is a model #> 146                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Update downsample logic for scuttle/tatami and fix tests (#129)\n\n* move to non-exact comparison\n\n* Updated downsampling C++ code to use new scuttle functions.\n\nAlso added some more checks to ensure we don't lose integer precision.\n\n* Stripped out test comparisons to downsampleMatrix.\n\nThese tests no longer make sense because the downsampling is no longer done on\na per-event basis (i.e. single UMIs or reads in each count). Rather, the new\nalgorithm operates on the entire count at once, for greater efficiency.\n\nThis all means that UMI and read counts are no longer interchangeable, which\nmeans that the results from downsampleReads/Matrix are no longer directly\ncomparable. This is okay - the test itself was highly contrived anyway as it\nonly works when every UMI has a single read.\n\n* Bumped version and date, updated NEWS.\n\n---------\n\nCo-authored-by: LTLA <infinite.monkeys.with.keyboards@gmail.com>

The static gene_symbol.txt lookup table\nonly mapped UCSC kgIDs to gene symbols, so all gene symbols resolved to NA.\n\nFix:\n- Update .txs2genesym() to handle both UCSC and Ensembl transcript IDs\n  - First tries static UCSC lookup table (backward compatible)\n  - Falls back to dynamic TxDb + org.Hs.eg.db lookup for Ensembl IDs\n- Pass genes TxDb to .txs2genesym() from eventDetection.R\n- Add AnnotationDbi to Imports, org.Hs.eg.db to Suggests\n- Replace dplyr::as_tibble with as.data.frame for Hits objects\n- Clean up vignette diagnostic code\n- Bump version to 1.17.5\n
